case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Children, Youth & Families Department v. Patricia H.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the termination, holding that CYFD's statutory obligation to make reasonable efforts to assist the parent is a prerequisite to termination, that what is reasonable varies with the parent's cooperation and the recalcitrance of the problems, and that the appellate task is limited to asking whether CYFD complied with the minimum required by law, which it did here.
key_cases.relevance: It is the New Mexico source of the reasonable-efforts formulation courts apply to a court-approved treatment plan, and it holds the assistance obligation is a condition precedent rather than an afterthought.
key_cases.quote: The statutory prerequisite of reasonable efforts to assist the parent must be satisfied before parental rights may be terminated

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Children, Youth & Families Department v. Athena H.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding that a mother's good-faith compliance with her treatment plan does not defeat termination where clear and convincing evidence shows she cannot safely parent within the foreseeable future, and that counsel was not ineffective.
key_cases.relevance: It is a leading New Mexico statement of the court-approved treatment plan's role and of CYFD's obligation to assist with it.
key_cases.quote: CYFD must provide reasonable efforts to assist the parent to change the conditions that gave rise to the neglect and abuse

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Children, Youth & Families Department v. Keon H. (In re Anhayla H.)
key_cases.holding: The Court held that substantial evidence supported the district court's finding that CYFD made reasonable efforts to assist an incarcerated father under Section 32A-4-28(B)(2), reversed the Court of Appeals, and affirmed the termination of his parental rights.
key_cases.relevance: It is the leading New Mexico Supreme Court statement on what a court-ordered treatment plan and CYFD's assistance with it must look like.
key_cases.quote: In this case, the Department's efforts, although imperfect, were reasonable.

key_cases.case_name: In the Matter of Grace H.
key_cases.holding: The Court held that where a parent is present and willing to participate before termination, abandonment must be pursued under Section 32A-4-28(B)(2), which requires CYFD assistance and treatment, rather than under Section 32A-4-28(B)(1); it reversed the termination and remanded.
key_cases.relevance: It ties the abandonment ground to the statutory requirement that the parent first be assessed and offered treatment under a plan.
key_cases.quote: we hold that where a parent is present and willing to participate prior to termination, termination by abandonment must follow from Subsection (B)(2)
